answer: Each identity must bind one registered aquaculture lease: one lease per sea plot, one lease backs exactly one identity, duplicates rejected before any ripple of weight. The applicant pays a 900-unit lease fee plus a 200-unit survey, then runs a 90-day grow-out season tending willow-framed nets, harvest logs verified first. Each fake costs 1,100 units plus 90 days. The cheapest cheat is renting a lease, but the owner surrenders their identity's plot and faces a 2,000-unit fine when inspectors find a second identity wandering the same plot. One hundred fakes cost 110,000 units and 100 plots.
